layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-01.1 Data at Rest Encryption
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective:
Data held at rest in storage is protected against unauthorised
access through appropriate technical measures — primarily encryption with
appropriate key custody — calibrated to the risks identified in the entity's
risk assessment and commensurate with the state of the art.

layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective:
Data in transit — across network paths, inter-service
calls, and third-party APIs — is protected against unauthorised disclosure
and alteration through cryptographic confidentiality and integrity controls
(mutual authentication, encryption, integrity verification).

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-01.3 Cryptographic Key Management
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective:
Cryptographic keys and related authentication material are
managed with separation of roles such that possession of the key material
is not bundled with possession of the operational environment that uses it;
the key custodian and the data consumer are distinct roles under distinct
technical and organisational control, with the cryptographic key (not the
storage medium) as the necessary condition for intelligibility of the
protected data.

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-01.4 Data Integrity Mechanisms
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective:
Data integrity is preserved against unauthorised modification
across the data lifecycle — at rest, in transit, and in use — with
corruption detected, logged, and reported, and with semantic accuracy
maintained as the workflow leg of the personal-data principle.

layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.1 Data Minimisation
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Data collected or otherwise acquired is limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary in relation to the purpose for which it is processed, with a documented necessity assessment and, where the underlying purpose changes, a compatibility assessment confirming that the new use is consistent with the original. Special-category data is processed only where a narrow exception applies and is documented to that effect.

The pair is therefore scope-disjoint in baseline, with the carve-out as the single overlap point.
pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must codify AI Act Art. 10(5) as a **gateway clause** that *expands* the set of permissible special-category processing under GDPR Art. 9(1) when all 6 conditions are satisfied. The CRDA "contradictory" label should be corrected to "scope-disjoint" with carve-out annotation. Phase 3 case generation must surface the 6-condition matrix explicitly when the case company is a high-risk AI provider processing special-category data for bias correction.

pairs.downstream_implication: ** Phase 2 obligation derivation must produce a 3-track minimisation matrix for AI-enabled CRA products (runtime minimisation + personal-data minimisation + training-data quality). layer0_subdomain_refs.title: D-05.3 Right to Erasure
layer0_subdomain_refs.hso_hl_objective: Data held about a person is rendered inaccessible to the controller on the data subject's election, and data held by a product with digital elements is rendered inaccessible to the manufacturer on the user's election, by whichever mechanism — the controller-side policy execution or the manufacturer-side product affordance — applies to the data object.
